title: Atomic structure
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:32Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank card covers protons, neutrons, electrons, atomic number and mass number well, but it never teaches that charge identifies an ion (protons minus electrons), which the new point's brief requires, so it is too narrow to reuse or adapt.

draft.title: Atomic structure
card: An atom has a nucleus of protons and neutrons, with electrons around it. Protons have a positive charge, electrons a negative charge, and neutrons have no charge.
the number of protons. It decides which element an atom is. Mass number is the number of protons plus neutrons.
atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons. They have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
a neutral atom has equal protons and electrons. An ion has gained or lost electrons, so its charge is protons minus electrons.
draft.remember: Protons name the element. Neutrons change the mass. Electrons change the charge.

a.q: How many neutrons are in an atom with atomic number 17 and mass number 35?
a.why: Neutrons = mass number minus atomic number = 35 - 17 = 18. The tempting answer 17 is the number of protons, not neutrons.
a.clue: Mass number counts protons and neutrons together.

b.q: An ion has 13 protons, 14 neutrons and 10 electrons. What is its charge and mass number?
b.why: Charge = protons minus electrons = 13 - 10 = 3+. Mass number = 13 + 14 = 27. Electrons are not counted in mass number, so 24 is wrong, and 3- reverses the charge.
b.clue: More protons than electrons means a positive charge.

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one clear right answer (18 neutrons; 3+ and mass number 27), and the card and explanations are accurate.
